findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:81 declares five registered discovery adapters, but buildResult assigns the same preassembled input.pathRefs to process_fact_registry, handler_dispatch_inventory, and static_call_graph, while runtime_trace performs no discovery. runAcceptanceDiscoveryAdapters only relabels this one input set; it never inspects handler/dispatch source, a static graph, or runtime facts. Because deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis constructs input.pathRefs from the topology/planned declarations themselves, the adapters cannot independently discover an omitted path or naturally disagree and can falsely classify the self-described closure complete. This violates Wave 1A's independent registered-adapter exit condition.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 53c949a2ec and 70e74b7b35: registered adapters now derive from separate canonical scope-contract, PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY, handler/dispatch registry source refs, static endpoint source inspection, and bounded runtime inputs rather than relabelling topology pathRefs. Current-HEAD focused smoke proves a real omitted registered consumer is discovered/fails closed and restored control passes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:160 computes closureFilesHash from only planned endpoint files; registered producer/consumer closure entries are appended as literal inventory strings and their referenced source files are never resolved or content-hashed. deriveRegisteredProcessFactClosure likewise emits producer/consumer labels rather than resolvable source paths (acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:44). Therefore an out-of-scope registered consumer can change while closureFilesHash remains unchanged, defeating the receipt freshness binding explicitly required by Wave 1A.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 53c949a2ec and 70e74b7b35: closureFilesHash now resolves and hashes content for every registered producer/consumer source ref, not literal labels; any missing/uninspectable source emits a blind spot and prevents complete. Current-HEAD closure-source content drift and closure-omission mutations bite, restored control passes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:278 contains the only topology-versus-basis and exclusion validation, but neither deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis nor the production generate/read handlers call it (handlers/proofstory.ts:134-184,206-234). Worse, derivation seeds every topology path into expectedPathRefs at lines 194-203 and the echo adapters reproduce it, so an invented topology path can be absorbed into a complete signed basis. The smoke calls reconcileTopologyWithCoverageBasis directly, which does not prove the real acceptance_basis_generate/acceptance_basis path rejects the mutation.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 53c949a2ec: production acceptance_basis_generate and acceptance_basis verification execute topology-versus-derived-basis reconciliation before accepting complete; topology is no longer adapter seed authority. Current-HEAD production invented-topology mutation fails through generate/read while legitimate planned topology passes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:289-291 implements exclusion eligibility as only a /^decision:/ string regex. It does not resolve the decisionRef from the canonical foundational decision store/schema, verify an eligible decision kind, or detect stale/unrelated decisions as required by CHK-004 and the plan. The smoke covers only free-form prose without a decision: prefix, so decision:anything would escape AT_UNJUSTIFIED_EXCLUSION. Add canonical decision resolution and negative tests for missing, stale, unrelated, and ineligible-kind refs (or explicitly leave all exclusions unsupported/non-complete in Wave 1A).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 53c949a2ec: exclusion decisionRefs are resolved against canonical foundational decision artifacts with schema, eligible kind, current relevance, uniqueness and target checks; regex-only acceptance removed. Current-HEAD valid/missing/stale/unrelated/ineligible/malformed/duplicate matrix yields stable AT_UNJUSTIFIED_EXCLUSION failures and restored valid control passes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:149-156 and :201-207 do not bind the discovered global closure source contents promised by closureFilesHash. computeClosureFilesHash hashes only files named by plannedPathRecords; sourceInventory entries for PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY producers/consumer gates are merely hashed as identifier strings and are never resolved to source files. A consumer outside Story scope can change without its file content entering closureFilesHash, violating the explicit Wave 1A requirement that every discovered producer and consumer source reference, including outside storyFilesHash, be content-bound and uninspectable consumers force partial.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 53c949a2ec and 70e74b7b35: discovered global producer/consumer source contents are included in canonical closureFilesHash and uninspectable entries force partial. Current-HEAD source-content drift, missing-source and out-of-scope consumer omission mutations invalidate freshness/completeness; restored control passes.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:194-204 and packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:81-108 do not implement independently derived discovery. deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis first takes path refs from the submitted topology/planned declarations, then buildResult copies that same precomputed set verbatim into process_fact_registry, handler_dispatch_inventory, and static_call_graph while runtime_trace contributes nothing. Consequently deleting an undeclared real handler/dispatch/static consumer from topology makes every synthetic adapter agree and can still yield status=complete; there is no repository/handler/dispatch/static/runtime inspection. This contradicts the Wave 1A exit condition and the new CLI promise that the registered profile derives the union. Implement method-specific adapters from canonical repository/runtime inputs and prove an actual omitted consumer is discovered/fails closed.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 53c949a2ec and 70e74b7b35: discovery no longer copies topology/planned pathRefs into every adapter; method-specific registered facts and repository source inspection independently derive the union. Current-HEAD removal of a real handler/dispatch/static consumer is detected, and bounded runtime trace cannot assert exhaustive completeness.

VI-A32A-001-CALLER-FORGERY explicitly requires every public entry point and status, enumeratedPathRefs, blindSpots, excludedPathRefs, generatedBy, and digest fields, including the direct handler boundary. No assertions cover the remaining fields, acceptance_basis_generate, or direct-handler rejection/ignore semantics, so its recorded manual_transcript is not sufficient.

Current-HEAD smoke covers 6 fields × 2 public commands × CLI and direct-handler boundaries, with atomic snapshots and restored controls.

VI-A32A-002-OMISSION-AND-AGGREGATE-TAMPER / VI-A32A-002-RESULT-AND-CLOSURE-TAMPER also require aggregate addition and blindSpot tamper, recomputed adapter digest retained under the old signed basis, and omission of the registered out-of-scope consumer from closure. It does not bite topologyDigest/version, scopeContractDigest, storyFilesHash, phaseBasis, adapter-set/result bindings, a freshly re-signed hash-only rebind, frozen topology/scope/discovery/story drift, or the legacy-missing/failed-generation no-partial-artifact/event guarantees required by VI-A32A-003-SIGNED-BOUND-RECEIPT, FRESHNESS-CLASSIFICATION, LEGACY-AND-ATOMICITY, and TAMPER-AND-HASH-REBIND. findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 53c949a2ec: current-HEAD smoke mutates receipt schema/topology digest+version/scope-check/scope-contract/head/material/storyFiles/closure/phase/adapter-set+results/story/workspace/signature, proves re-signed hash-only rebind rejection, frozen input drift, legacy missing behavior and failed-generation no-partial-artifact/event atomicity; restored receipts verify.

findings.desc: CHK-004/005 strict coverage is incomplete: packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:174-186 tests deletion, one invented existing ref, free-form exclusion prose, and invalid file only. It does not retain declaration IDs while drifting endpoint role/artifact/file/symbol/relation/output fact, nor test valid vs malformed/stale/duplicate/unrelated/ineligible-kind decisionRefs as required by the frozen plan and VI-A32A-004-*. Lines 218-237 exercise JSON reads only and snapshot only artifact after invalid input, not text rendering plus full story/events/git/lifecycle atomicity; verify-process-fact-contract is only run green, with no one-sided registration mutation required by VI-A32A-005-PROCESS-FACT-CONTRACT. findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:164-180 still does not implement an independently enumerating handler/dispatch inventory or static call graph: both adapters iterate only closure.entries already selected from PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY using planned-path seeds, then use substring presence to mark each known entry inspectable. runAcceptanceDiscoveryAdapters at lines 210-214 supplies no checklist/scope file inventory, so an unregistered handler/consumer (or any Story with no plannedPathRecords) is never scanned and produces neither a path nor a blind spot. The basis can therefore call the discovery profile complete while an omitted C2 outside that preselected registry closure is invisible; F-001's independent discovery requirement remains unresolved.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f4de47a239: discovery no longer starts from the planned/process-fact closure. Scope obligations, full PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY candidates, command-catalog plus exact registry.registerBatch handler dispatches, static producer/consumer source inspection, and RUNTIME_FACT_REGISTRY are independently enumerated. Current-HEAD smoke deletes real dispatch registration and adds comment-only/token-mismatch controls; both fail partial before restored control passes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:339-348 enforces topology mapping only for planned: and path:existing: entries. Paths actually emitted by the repaired registry/runtime adapters use path:process-fact: and path:runtime-fact:, so they bypass AT_UNMAPPED_SCOPE_REF entirely; the reverse topology loop also cannot map those encodings. A globally discovered consumer can therefore remain absent from topology/exclusions without making the basis partial, contrary to the required registered-consumer closure invariant.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f4de47a239: reconciliation normalizes and maps every discovered encoding, including process-fact and runtime-fact paths, in both basis-to-topology and topology-to-basis directions. Current-HEAD unmapped process/runtime consumer and reverse omission mutations produce AT_UNMAPPED_SCOPE_REF/AT_TOPOLOGY_OUTSIDE_BASIS; restored mappings pass.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:117-143 and :164-171 still do not mechanically verify handler/dispatch registration. handlerInspectable marks every producerSourceRef inspectable when each file contains any generic entry token; for acceptance_basis_generate, registry.ts can continue matching proofstory/acceptance-basis comments or imports even after registry.registerBatch(createProofStoryHandlers(ctx)) is deleted. The adapter then emits the registered process-fact path and can agree with the registry adapter, so a real dispatch omission can remain complete. The current smoke only mutates an already-built result to empty and never deletes the real dispatch registration. Parse/resolve the canonical registry/command-to-handler binding (or fail partial) and add a production-source omission mutation.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f4de47a239: handler/dispatch inspectability requires exact command-catalog name, exact registry.registerBatch(createProofStoryHandlers(ctx)) binding and exact proofstory handler method, not generic token presence. Current-HEAD production-source dispatch deletion and comment/import token decoys fail; restored registration passes.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:131-134 and :172-179 contradict the Wave 1A PLAN semantics for genuinely new endpoints. plannedInspectable requires every declared producer/consumer symbol to already occur in a source file, and static_call_graph turns any not-yet-created PLAN endpoint into a blind spot; deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis then classifies the basis partial. The plan and CHK-004 explicitly require a valid frozen planned declaration to enter a complete PLAN basis even when symbols do not yet exist. The smoke writes producer.ts/consumer.ts before deriving and therefore misses this case. Treat valid in-scope planned declarations as structural PLAN obligations without requiring implementation symbols, while preserving pre-REVIEW actual reconciliation for Wave 3, and add a no-files-yet PLAN control.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f4de47a239: valid frozen in-scope planned declarations are structural PLAN obligations and no longer require not-yet-created files/symbols, while registered/existing actual discovery remains independently inspected. Current-HEAD no-files-yet PLAN control completes and invalid/unresolved declarations still fail closed.

findings.desc: CHK-002 evidence remains incomplete after F-008 repair. packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:169-181 and 200-216 cover cardinality, path/digest, one disagreement, and closure omission, but VI-A32A-002-PROFILE-TOTALITY and VI-A32A-002-RESULT-AND-CLOSURE-TAMPER also require invalid coverage claim, provenance, blind spot, and asymmetry-policy cases plus proof that caller discoveryMethods cannot narrow the registered profile. The current smoke contains no discoveryMethods case and only changes pathRefs/one coverageClaim optimism case, so two must intents are still semantically under-covered.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f4de47a239: current-HEAD matrix now bites invalid coverage claim, provenance, blindSpot completeness, asymmetry kind/policyRef/scopeRefs and caller discoveryMethods narrowing; shuffled registered results remain canonical. Each mutation asserts its intended partial/error and restored control passes.

findings.desc: CHK-003 caller/freshness evidence remains incomplete after F-009 repair. The forbidden-field matrix at packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:333-345 omits receiptRef, basisDigest, issuer identity, signature, and the individual binding-hash fields explicitly required by VI-A32A-003-CALLER-ISSUER-FORGERY. The receipt mutation matrix proves signed tamper rejection, but VI-A32A-003-FRESHNESS-CLASSIFICATION separately requires headHash-only and unrelated-material movement to be classified by the existing freshness reader and never silently rebound; no such classification controls exist. Thus the two recorded pass rows still overclaim their must intents.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f4de47a239 plus b926319a11/9fb0dd5f24 contract correction: both public strict schemas and direct handlers reject receiptRef, basisDigest, issuer/signature and every individual binding hash in addition to inventory fields. Current-HEAD freshness controls classify head-only and unrelated-material/storyFilesHash-unchanged movement through the canonical reader without rebinding or artifact mutation.

findings.desc: CHK-005 evidence remains incomplete after F-010 repair. VI-A32A-005-LEGACY-UNSUPPORTED-DETERMINISM requires real-CLI legacy-missing, partial, and unsupported cases plus shuffled-equivalent adapter inputs; the smoke has real legacy/partial paths but unsupported only at the pure reconciliation layer and no shuffled adapter-order replay. VI-A32A-005-READONLY-DIAGNOSTIC-BOUNDARY requires rendered output to be rejected when replayed as gate evidence/authority, not merely labeled non-evidentiary. VI-A32A-005-PROCESS-FACT-CONTRACT requires omission/one-sided prompt, handler, registry, or contract registration mutations, while lines 475-487 exercise only drop-acceptance-basis-registry. Three must evidence rows therefore remain incomplete.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by f4de47a239, 9fb0dd5f24 and b926319a11: current-HEAD production CLI covers legacy missing/partial/unsupported and shuffled deterministic replay; diagnostic output is rejected as authority; prompt/handler/registry/contract one-sided mutations each fail then restored contract passes. Prompt side is the lattice-implementer sole-writer/read-only/non-authority boundary; writer command/artifact are L3 non-gate, explicitly preventing Wave2 enforcement.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:61-84 and :182-195 leave F-011 unresolved. handler_dispatch_inventory and static_call_graph independently perform exact checks only after relevantProcessFacts filters PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY by terms copied from plannedPathRecords; neither adapter enumerates checklist/scope source files or discovers handlers/consumers absent from that preselected registry subset. Therefore an unregistered real handler/consumer C2, or a Story with no plannedPathRecords, yields no path and no blind spot and can still classify complete. Exact validation of known entries fixed F-013 but is not independent enumeration. Build a bounded source inventory from canonical checklist/scope files, enumerate handler/dispatch/static relations independently of topology/planned terms, union with registered closure, and add a real undeclared/unregistered C2 omission mutation.

doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:67-72 and :135-195 still do not implement a general independently enumerated handler/dispatch/static discovery adapter. Candidate entries are restricted to PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY rows keyword-matched from plannedPathRecords; the dispatch verifier is then hard-coded to command-catalog.ts, createProofStoryHandlers(ctx), and handlers/proofstory.ts. It neither scans signed scope/checklist source files for additional consumers nor follows each registry entry's actual owner/source refs, so non-ProofStory commands such as the plan's review_run_start example can never be confirmed while an unregistered extra consumer remains invisible rather than producing a blind spot. The owner claim that f4de47a239 enumerates full registry/scope candidates is not supported by the production source; F-011's generic Wave 1A discovery requirement remains incomplete.

doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:106-181 builds its reverse-import universe only from signed scope seed files plus already-declared PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY source refs. A consumer outside Story scope that is not already listed in producerSourceRefs/consumerSourceRefs is never scanned and creates no blind spot; reached entries also no longer fail partial when consumerGate exists but consumerSourceRefs is absent. The generic smoke at proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:372-374 calls C2 external but explicitly adds packages/main/src/consumers/c2.ts to scopeRefs, so it does not prove the required outside-scope consumer closure. Removing that scope ref makes C2 invisible while the bounded discovery can remain complete. F-019/Wave 1A's global registered-consumer requirement is therefore still unresolved.

Canonical source-root inventory does not fail closed when an intermediate scanRoot/rootDir component is a symlink that escapes the workspace. configuredSourceInventory validates only the lexical resolve/relative result (lines 117-120) and lstatSync(absoluteRoot) on the final path (lines 121-128). lstat on /workspace/link/src follows the intermediate link, so with scanRoot=link, rootDir=src, and link -> /outside, the external /outside/src directory is accepted and enumerated as if canonical workspace source. No realpath containment or component-by-component symlink check exists. The added smoke covers only a missing root (lines 431-433), not malformed/escaping/root-symlink/unreadable roots. This violates the targeted F-020 repair requirement that escaping and symlinked canonical roots yield partial. Bind workspace and source-root realpaths, reject any root whose physical path escapes the physical workspace or traverses a symlink/ambiguous component, and add adversarial controls for parent-component symlink escape plus malformed, lexical escape, and unreadable roots.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 39a348ddcf and retained through current HEAD: canonical roots use physical per-component containment with symlink/escape failures, and TypeScript-aware executable call discovery excludes literal/comment/template-static decoys. Current mutation smoke and round-13 formal coverage PASS.

findings.desc: The canonical source-root scan still does not establish an exact executable import-and-call edge. exactCalledImports and staticCallPaths strip comments and import declarations but leave string and template literal contents, then accept any alias followed by an opening parenthesis regex match (acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:176-180, 308-312, 327-331). Therefore an outside-scope file that imports a producer but only contains a string such as const marker = consume( is added to the closure, emitted as a static-call path, and can satisfy discoveredConsumer even though it never calls the producer. Focused reproduction against the same stripping and matching algorithm printed {executableText: export const marker = consume(, classifiedAsCall:true}. The new smoke covers a real call, removal, unresolved import, and unrelated file, but has no string or template false-positive mutation (proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:369-423). This leaves F-020 no-false-exclusion and exact-import-call condition open. Use syntax-aware call-expression binding or conservatively fail partial when the bounded parser cannot prove a call, and add a mutation where the alias appears only inside string or template text and must not enter closure or satisfy the consumer gate.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 39a348ddcf and retained through current HEAD: canonical roots use physical per-component containment with symlink/escape failures, and TypeScript-aware executable call discovery excludes literal/comment/template-static decoys. Current mutation smoke and round-13 formal coverage PASS.

findings.desc: The new lexicalCodeMask still does not model JavaScript regular-expression literals, so F-022 remains open for both false-positive and false-negative edges. At acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:364-390, slash is handled only for line and block comments; ordinary regex content is copied as executable code and a closing brace inside a regex is treated as the end of a template interpolation. The unchanged alias-call regex at lines 196-200 and 410-415 therefore classifies `const p=/consumeReviewRun(foo)/;` as a real imported call, while a real call in `${/}/.test(v) ? consumeReviewRun() : false}` is masked after the regex brace. A focused reproduction using the exact mask printed the first case classifiedAsCall:true and the second classifiedAsCall:false. The smoke at proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:390-414 covers comments, quoted strings, static template text, and a simple interpolation only; it has no regex-literal mutation. This can still invent an outside-scope consumer or omit a real interpolated consumer and incorrectly satisfy or fail the completeness claim. Parse call expressions with a syntax-aware scanner, or conservatively emit a blind spot when regex versus division cannot be proven; add both regex mutations and restored real-call controls.

The canonical source inventory is still not actually bounded by MAX_SOURCE_INVENTORY_FILES. In configuredSourceInventory at acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:148-168, every qualifying file is pushed before the size check, and exceeding 20,000 returns only from the current recursive visit call. Each parent visit continues its remaining siblings and later subdirectories, so files keeps growing and the whole tree can still be traversed and retained in memory; only the final returned projection is sliced. A repository with more than 20,000 source files can therefore consume work proportional to the full tree despite the advertised safety bound, with repeated over-limit pushes before stable deduplication. The new smoke adds path, symlink, malformed-config, and unreadable-root cases but no over-limit tree or early-stop assertion (proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:457-495). Propagate a global stopped state or iterative traversal break immediately at the cap, retain one deterministic blind spot, and prove that files or directories after the bound are never visited or accumulated.

AST discovery still does not prove that a direct-call identifier is bound to the imported producer. analyzeLocalImportCalls records imported local names at acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:250-261, then collects every CallExpression identifier by text across all scopes at lines 263-269. Legal shadowing such as `import { emitReviewRunFact as consumeReviewRun } from ../handlers/review-run.js; export const c2 = (consumeReviewRun: () => boolean) => consumeReviewRun();` parses cleanly but the only call targets the parameter, not the import; the current calledNames/intersection nevertheless emits the producer->C2 edge, enters C2 into closure, and can satisfy consumerGate as complete. The added AST smoke covers regex/template/parse/size cases but no shadow-binding mutation (proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:391-440). This violates the exact imported direct-call condition and reopens false completeness. Resolve the identifier binding with a TypeScript Program/type checker or a conservative lexical scope tracker, fail partial when binding cannot be proven, and add parameter/local/function/catch shadow mutations plus a restored imported-call control.

The new global directory budget is deterministic but has an exact-boundary off-by-one that reports partial before consuming the last permitted directory. In enumerateBoundedSourceTree, after visiting the root stats.directories is 1; when it encounters the sole child with maxDirectories=2, line 154 tests `1 + 0 + 0 >= 2` and stops instead of enqueueing/visiting that second allowed directory. Thus a tree whose total directory count exactly equals maxDirectories is classified exhausted/partial although it is within the declared maximum. The smoke proves an exact maxFiles boundary but only proves directory exhaustion is <= cap; it has no exact maxDirectories complete control. Change the child scheduling guard so equality is allowed while the next directory beyond the cap stops globally, and add exact-boundary plus one-over directory cases.

AST parsing fixes regex and template lexing, but imported-call exactness is still name-only rather than binding-aware. acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:263-269 collects every identifier CallExpression text into one file-wide Set and marks an import called when its local name appears anywhere. Valid nested shadowing therefore invents a consumer: `import { emit as consume } from ./producer.js; function wrapper(consume) { return consume(); }` has zero parse diagnostics and calledNames=[consume], although the imported binding is never called. That false edge can add an outside-scope file to closure and satisfy discoveredConsumer. The focused AST reproduction printed parseDiagnostics:0, calledNames:[consume], importedBindingActuallyCalled:false. Current smoke tests aliases and syntax forms but has no shadowed parameter, local binding, catch binding, or nested-scope mutation. Resolve each call identifier to the actual ImportSpecifier or ImportClause symbol, or conservatively mark shadowed/unprovable bindings partial, and add shadowing mutations plus a restored imported alias call.

Canonical inventory and module resolution silently omit source kinds that the scanner claims or TypeScript supports. SOURCE_EXTENSIONS at acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:83 excludes .jsx, .mts, and .cts even though scriptKindFor at lines 231-235 has an otherwise unreachable JSX branch and the profile is TypeScript-based. resolveLocalImport at lines 112-121 only maps .js to .ts plus bare .ts/index.ts, so imports resolving to .tsx/.jsx/.mts/.cts are also missed. Conversely .cjs is inventoried and parsed as JS, but analyzeLocalImportCalls at lines 252-261 recognizes only ES ImportDeclaration and neither CommonJS require nor TypeScript import-equals; those consumers are silently ignored without an unsupported-source blind spot. If another valid consumer already satisfies consumerGate, an additional outside-scope C2 in any omitted form disappears while the basis can remain complete. The smoke contains only a .ts named ES import and has no source-extension/module-form matrix. Either fully support the declared canonical source kinds and Node/TS resolution or emit deterministic partial blind spots for unsupported extensions/forms; add outside-scope .jsx/.mts/.cts and .cjs require mutations proving omission cannot remain complete.

F-024 global counters now stop queued traversal, but maxEntries still does not bound the expensive operation it is meant to protect. enumerateBoundedSourceTree calls readdirSync(...withFileTypes).sort(...) at acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:143-145 before inspecting maxEntries at lines 147-149. A single adversarial directory with millions of entries is therefore fully materialized and sorted in memory before the 100,000-entry stop can fire; pending work and CPU/memory remain proportional to the unbounded directory, not the configured budget. The new budget smoke uses only small directories and asserts counters after enumeration, so it cannot detect this pre-budget allocation (proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:526-557). Use bounded incremental directory iteration with an explicit per-directory/entry stop before retaining or sorting beyond the remaining budget, or fail closed through a separately bounded inventory primitive, and add a high-fanout mutation proving the iterator never materializes or visits beyond remainingEntries+1.

Unreadable individual source files are not converted into deterministic partial evidence. enumerateBoundedSourceTree only lstat checks size and inventories the file at acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:160-169; analyzeLocalImportCalls then performs an unguarded readFileSync at lines 238-242. A permission-denied file, directory/file race, or transient I/O error throws out of runAcceptanceDiscoveryAdapters instead of returning the required uninspectable blind spot and partial basis. The only unreadability smoke chmods the configured root directory itself, which is rejected earlier by mode bits, so it does not exercise an unreadable inventoried file (proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts:511-519). Catch file reads and parse construction, emit a stable source-file-unreadable blind spot, and add an individual chmod/race-shaped mutation with restored control.

The expanded local-module matrix still silently omits valid direct CommonJS/dynamic local module calls that are not first assigned to a VariableDeclaration. visitRequires only creates bindings from variable declarations (acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:424-445), while call discovery only accepts Identifier, Identifier.property, or Identifier[string] callees (lines 447-470). Therefore `exports.c2 = () => require(../handlers/review-run.js).emitReviewRunFact()` has an outer PropertyAccess whose base is a CallExpression and produces neither a binding, unresolved-module blind spot, nor an edge; similarly `const m = await import(...); m.emitReviewRunFact()` and direct `(await import(...)).emitReviewRunFact()` are silently invisible. If another registered consumer exists, these additional outside-scope consumers can be omitted while basis remains complete. The smoke proves destructured/identifier require and import-equals only. Either support inline require/dynamic-import property calls and binding flows, or emit deterministic unsupported-module-form blind spots so the basis is partial; add direct inline require, assigned dynamic import, and direct awaited dynamic import mutations.

The advertised 2 MiB lexical-source budget is checked only after the entire file has already been read into memory. readSourceSafely calls readFileSync(descriptor, utf8) at acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:324 before createBindingAnalysisContext applies MAX_LEXICAL_SOURCE_BYTES at lines 345-349; sourceProvenance also calls readSourceSafely without applying that lexical cap. A static 50–90 MiB source still fits the 100 MiB inventory budget and is fully allocated/read before being classified partial, and a TOCTOU growth after inventory lstat can make the read arbitrarily larger before the post-read inode/size check rejects it. Thus F-029 bounded-work semantics and F-030 TOCTOU handling are outcome-fail-closed but not resource-bounded. Check opened-fd fstat size against the per-file cap before reading, use a bounded read that detects one byte over cap, and ensure provenance reuses the bounded snapshot; add instrumentation proving oversized and growth-race cases never read beyond cap+1.

The 2 MiB lexical budget is enforced only after the complete file has already been allocated. readSourceSafely performs readFileSync(descriptor, utf8) at acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:315-324 without checking opened.size against MAX_LEXICAL_SOURCE_BYTES; createBindingAnalysisContext checks Buffer.byteLength only afterward at lines 343-348. The analysis input also unions inventory with seedFiles and registryCandidates at lines 501-502, so planned/scope/registered files can bypass the inventory aggregate byte/file caps entirely; an oversized seed or a file grown after traversal can force an arbitrarily large read before becoming partial. The current oversized smoke proves post-read classification, not pre-allocation boundedness. Check fstat size before read, reject growth beyond a bounded descriptor read, and apply aggregate analysis file/byte budgets to every union source. Also define fail-closed behavior when O_NOFOLLOW is unavailable rather than reading a raced symlink target before later identity checks.

The TypeChecker comparison is exact only after a binding has been classified, but classification/call extraction still has silent false edges. requireSpecifier at acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:419-445 accepts any identifier text named require without checking its symbol, so a locally declared `function require(){...}` plus `const { emit } = require(./producer.js); emit()` is falsely treated as a CommonJS producer import; a focused TypeChecker probe confirms that shadowed require has its own local symbol. Conversely the call visitor at lines 447-470 recognizes only bare Identifier, PropertyAccess, and string ElementAccess callees, so real direct calls through valid transparent TS wrappers such as `(consume)()`, `consume!()`, and `(consume as Fn)()` are silently omitted; the AST probe reports ParenthesizedExpression/NonNullExpression rather than Identifier. Optional bare calls work, but these variants are untested. Validate require against the intended unshadowed CommonJS binding or fail partial, recursively unwrap semantically transparent call expressions before symbol equality, and add false-require plus wrapped-call mutations.

Local module resolution validates physical containment but returns the caller-spelled candidate path rather than the canonical physical relative path. At acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:127-162, physicallyContainedRegularFile resolves the real target only to return boolean; viable retains `rel` derived from the lexical candidate. On a case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing filesystem, an import with casing/normalization different from the on-disk filename can therefore yield exactly one viable sourceFile spelled differently from sourceInventory.files and seed paths. The import is reported resolved with no blind spot, yet closure equality misses the real producer or consumer; on a case-sensitive host the same import becomes partial, creating cross-host nondeterminism. Return the canonical relative path derived from realpathSync, reject or explicitly diagnose spelling collisions/case drift, use locale-independent ordering, and add case/normalization mutations appropriate to each platform.

Directory traversal still has a TOCTOU gap that can omit a new consumer or follow a swapped directory outside the canonical root. enumerateBoundedSourceTree queues child path strings from Dirent state, then later calls opendirSync(directory) at acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:180-203 without re-lstat/realpath containment or before/after directory identity and mtime checks. A queued child replaced with a symlink can be followed by opendirSync and expose external names/sizes; a consumer added, removed, or renamed while the iterator runs can be absent from the admitted deterministic set without any blind spot. File-level readSourceSafely may later reject external content, but it does not detect an omitted concurrent entry, so completeness can be issued over a non-snapshot inventory. Revalidate each directory immediately before open without following symlinks, compare identity/change metadata after iteration, fail partial on mutation, and add directory swap plus add/remove-during-iteration mutations with handle-close assertions.

Dynamic-import namespace bindings are incorrectly classified as directly callable default imports, leaving a false-completeness edge in the F-031 repair. moduleCall correctly identifies `await import(./producer.js)` as kind=import (acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:538-550), but visitModuleBindings passes every identifier binding to addBinding as imported=`default`, direct=true, property=true whenever there is no selected property (lines 566-580). Thus valid syntax `const review = await import(../handlers/review-run.js); review();` has no parse ambiguity; the checker resolves review to that binding and lines 606-613 emit a static call edge to producer#default even though an ESM module namespace object is not callable and no producer export is invoked. This can enter an outside-scope C2 and satisfy consumerGate as complete. The smoke covers review.emitReviewRunFact(), destructuring, and direct import().property(), but not a direct call of the namespace variable. Classify assigned dynamic import as imported=*, direct=false, property=true (while destructured/property-selected bindings remain direct), optionally surface semantic non-callability as partial, and add namespace-direct-call false-edge plus restored property-call controls.

Inline CommonJS support handles `require(./module).property()` but still silently omits the callable-module form `require(./producer)()`. In the call visitor, propertyModuleCall only recognizes PropertyAccess/ElementAccess over a module call (acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:553-565, 587-594); for the outer call in `require(./producer)()`, node.expression is itself a CallExpression, so no target or directProperty is produced. The inner require call is not a VariableDeclaration binding and there is no unsupported-require blind spot, allowing a valid CommonJS `module.exports = function producer(){}` consumer to disappear while another consumer keeps basis complete. The implementation already treats `const producer = require(...); producer()` as direct/default-callable, so inline equivalence is an internal semantic inconsistency. Recognize a moduleCall as the outer callee and emit its default/export= edge, or conservatively mark that require shape partial; add inline callable-module and shadowed-require controls.

The new shared SourceReadContext does not reach the final closure hash read, so F-033 remains open on the production derivation path. deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis calls computeClosureFilesHash at acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:231-242 after discovery; computeClosureFilesHash independently maps every planned/inventory file and calls unbounded, no-follow-unprotected readFileSync at lines 178-187. A huge seed/closure file, symlink swap, permission race, or aggregate file set can therefore allocate or escape the adapter budget again and may throw before the already-partial basis is returned. Its bytes can also differ from the cached snapshots used by adapter provenance, producing a mixed-time receipt binding. Pass the same canonical bounded snapshots/digests into closure hashing or expose a bounded verifier-owned hash result with diagnostics; never reread paths independently. Add a production deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis mutation proving oversized/swapped/disappearing closure files return deterministic partial without a second allocation or throw.

The directory hardening still has resource and snapshot gaps. At acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:228-230, closeSync failure is swallowed without the promised blind spot, handlesClosed remains short, and the collected rows can still be admitted, so an actual close error can leak a descriptor yet yield complete. At lines 231-243 a changed directory discards rows and continues without charging rows.length to stats.entries or stopping; up to maxDirectories mutated directories can each consume remainingEntries+1 reads, bypassing the global entry-work budget by orders of magnitude. Finally, directories are checked only immediately around their own read, so a previously accepted directory can change later while other directories are scanned and produce a mixed-time inventory with no final revalidation. Treat close failure and any directory mutation as a global stop, charge iterator work independently of admitted entries, retain and revalidate every accepted directory snapshot before returning, and add injected close failure plus mutation-after-earlier-directory tests.

The new immutable content cache does not preserve a single workspace-membership/content snapshot through graph, provenance, closure hash, and return. enumerateBoundedSourceTree performs its final directory revalidation only inside enumeration (acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:305-320) and returns only files/blindSpots, discarding admittedDirectories. buildBoundedSourceGraph then reads and analyzes those files afterward (lines 726-795), and runAcceptanceDiscoverySnapshot builds adapters/provenance and returns cached contents still later (lines 951-971), with no final directory or per-file identity revalidation. A C2 created after configuredSourceInventory returns is absent from boundedUniverse and can coexist at receipt issuance with status complete; likewise a cached consumer changed after its read remains the graph/provenance/hash truth even though the workspace now differs. The added mutation test fires before the enumerator final revalidation, so it cannot bite this post-enumeration/post-read window. Retain directory and opened-file snapshot identities in the discovery snapshot and revalidate all of them after adapter/provenance/hash assembly (or bind to an immutable git/object snapshot); any drift must make the same derivation partial and discard complete. Add hooks that add a C2 after inventory return and mutate an early-read C2 before runAcceptanceDiscoverySnapshot returns.

acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:323-375 still derives the source universe from an unfrozen, unbounded configuration input: it follows and readFileSyncs lattice.config.json at line 328, then calls loadConfig at line 343, whose separate read/cache path is config.ts:689-723. The path is never lstat/no-follow checked, size-budgeted, content-digested, or included in the shared AcceptanceSourceSnapshot. A symlinked/external config or a change/cache mismatch between these reads can let the first JSON validation and the actual scanRoot/rootDir describe different source roots; discovery may then freeze a complete graph for the wrong/narrow universe, and the closure hash binds no config content. This is distinct from F-041’s post-enumeration mutation window: it corrupts the universe before enumeration begins. Read the canonical config once through the same bounded no-follow snapshot discipline, parse that exact content (without a second cached load), bind its digest, and add symlink/oversize/two-read mutation tests that must force partial rather than complete.

acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:1082-1087 invokes the caller-provided testHooks.afterSeal callback after sealSourceAssembly has completed every directory/file revalidation but before its blindSpots are returned; acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:312-319 then trusts that already-computed empty list and can classify complete. Concrete repro: pass discoveryTestHooks.afterSeal that writes packages/main/src/late-after-seal.ts (or mutates producer.ts). The callback executes at line 1086 after the final fingerprints were checked, seal() still returns [], and deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis returns status complete while the workspace no longer matches its inventory/provenance/hash. Because discoveryTestHooks is part of the exported derivation input, this is an actual deterministic bypass of the new final seal, not merely a scheduling hypothesis. Remove any mutation-capable callback after the last check (or perform an additional final validation after it) and add the exact afterSeal write mutation assertion that status must be partial.

The end-of-assembly seal is not independently bound into the basis verifier. deriveAcceptanceCoverageBasis appends discovery.seal() output only to the aggregate basis.blindSpots (acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:312-317), while verifyAcceptanceCoverageBasis reconstructs only adapter-result blind spots and accepts every remaining string by a broad prefix regex (lines 335-340). Consequently the new late-C2 partial fixture can be mutated by deleting its `directory changed before derivation seal` blind spot, setting status='complete', and recomputing basisDigest; because its pre-seal adapter results reconcile complete, verifyAcceptanceCoverageBasis returns ok=true. Conversely a complete basis accepts an attacker-authored `source file forged...` blind spot when status is changed to partial and the basis is re-digested. The existing aggregate blind-spot mutation test uses a non-whitelisted prefix (smoke.ts:348-351), so it does not exercise this bypass. Represent seal observations as a canonical digest-bound result (or another mechanically reconstructible signed projection) and require exact projection equality; add mutations for both allowed-prefix forgery and removal of a real seal blind spot, with the latter required to keep verification non-ok after re-digesting.
